entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Daya Ram Sharma, learned counsel for the appellant.

Ms. Abha Mishra- P.P. appearing on behalf of Advocate General.
 Shri Rajiv Jain, learned counsel for the Respondent [COMP].
I.A. No. 15422/2022, an application under section 5 of Limitation Act for condonation of delay in filing the instant appeal is taken up, considered and allowed for the reasons mentioned therein.
Delay of 91 days in filing the instant appeal is hereby condoned.
Also heard on the question of admission.
This appeal appears to be arguable, hence, it is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No. 17592 of 2022, which is Ist application under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved by the sole appellant - Shivnandan Sharma.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 27.04.2022 passed by Special Judge (POCSO Act),
District Guna in Special Case No. SC/66/2017, whereby appellant has been convicted and sentenced to undergo imprisonment as under:-
Conviction U/s Sentence Fine (in Rs.) Default (in lieu of fine) 363 of IPC 2 years RI 500/- One Month RI 366 of IPC 2 years RI 500/- One Month RI 376 (1) of IPC 10 years RI 1,000/- Three months RI 6 of POCSO Act Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted the appellant ignoring the evidence available on record.
He further argued that as per prosecution story, the date of birth of the prosecutrix is stated to be 04/10/1998 and incident occurred in the year 2016
, therefore, learned court below has wrongly assessed the age of the prosecutrix below 18 years, whereas, her age was around 18 years on the date of incident.

It is further argued that the prosecutrix has not been examined as she died before her statement is recorded before the court below and only on the basis of her previous statement, appellant has been convicted in the present case.

The appellant Shivnandan Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77072550/
1 has already served total incarceration of around 15 months out of total awarded imprisonment of 10 years.

entities.text: Shivnandan Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are material omissions and contradictions in the evidence of prosecution witnesses.
No active role of the present appellant has been proved by the prosecution in commission of offence.
Final hearing of this appeal will take long time.
Hence, prayed to suspend the jail sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Counsel for the State as well as counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials available on record.
Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, without commenting on merits of the case, I.A.No. 17592 of 2022 is hereby allowed.

Subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.
The appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the Office of this Court on 26/10/2023 and on subsequent dates given by the Office in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
A copy of this order be sent to the concerned Court below for compliance.

Certified copy/ e-copy as per rules/directions.
(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE Durgekar Shivnandan Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77072550/
